findings.title: Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a syntax error. Rendering `/embed/best` after a topic exists will raise ActionView::Template::Error instead of showing the discussion. It must be `<% end %>`.

findings.title: Feed poll crashes when an item has no content
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a non-nil `content` string. SimpleRSS items often only set `description` (or neither). The first such item raises NoMethodError, aborts the rest of the feed, and — with `retry: false` — drops the hourly import until the next run. Nil-check and fall back to `description` before unescaping.

findings.title: raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML
findings.body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, skipping the normal Sanitize/PrettyText pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` writes RSS item HTML (and Readability output) with that cook method, and `embed/best.html.erb` prints it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The same cooked HTML is what the main topic page serves. An RSS item can therefore inject script or event-handler markup into every viewer of the imported topic. RSS bodies need the same tag/attribute allowlist (and `javascript:` URL rejection) as the rest of post cooking before they are stored.

findings.title: Embed URL is interpolated into HTML unescaped
findings.body: The imported-from footer builds `#{url}` and then stores the string as raw HTML. The only check is `/^https?:\/\//`, so a URL such as `http://host/' onclick='alert(1)` or one containing `<` breaks out of the attribute/text and becomes stored XSS in the post and the embed iframe. Escape the URL for both the href attribute and the link text.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL
findings.body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the full referring page URL. `postMessage`'s targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`). A path-bearing referer does not match the parent origin, so browsers drop the message (or throw) and the parent iframe never receives `discourse-resize`. Height will stay at the default and the embed will clip. Pass only the referer origin.

findings.title: Resize message origin check is inverted and too loose
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts the message whenever `e.origin` is any substring of `discourseUrl`, including the empty string (sandboxed/data iframes, where `origin` is `""` and `indexOf` returns 0). It does not require `e.origin` to equal the Discourse origin. Any such frame can set the embed iframe height. Compare parsed origins for equality instead.

findings.title: Remote fetch follows redirects off the embeddable host
findings.body: `TopicRetriever` only checks that `URI(embed_url).host` equals `embeddable_host`, then `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read`. open-uri follows redirects by default, so a page on the allowed host (or a query-string URL an attacker can get that host to serve) can 302 to an internal address (`http://127.0.0.1`, cloud metadata, etc.). The Sidekiq worker will request that target and import the body as a topic. Disable redirects or re-check the host after each hop, and do the same for `PollFeed`'s `open(feed_polling_url)`.

findings.title: Every embed miss enqueues a fetch with no host or dedupe check
findings.body: `best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any `embed_url` as soon as no `TopicEmbed` row exists. It never checks that the URL's host is `embeddable_host` (that check is only inside the job) and does not dedupe. A page on the allowed host, or repeated views while the topic is still missing, fills the queue; if `embed_by_username` is blank or the fetch fails, nothing is created and `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30s forever. Validate the host before enqueue and avoid enqueueing when a recent attempt already failed.

findings.title: Disqus import now depends on a live HTTP fetch
findings.body: The importer used to create the topic from the XML export. It now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which `open`s `t[:link]` with no rescue. A dead, redirected, or non-HTML link raises and aborts the whole XML import; even a soft failure (`post` blank) silently skips every comment on that thread. Network errors need to be isolated per thread, with a fallback topic so comments are not dropped.
